title: Pro-Swedish Poland
capsule: Pro-Swedish Poland designates the regime of Stanisław I Leszczyński (Stanisław Leszczyński), installed as king of Poland in 1704 by a pro-Swedish faction in the Warsaw Confederation after Augustus II of Saxony was declared deposed, and supported throughout by Charles XII of Sweden during the Great Northern War. Stanisław was crowned in Warsaw in September 1705 and signed the Treaty of Warsaw, aligning Poland against Russia. Charles XII's decisive defeat of Augustus in Saxony produced the Peace of Altranstädt (14 September 1706), forcing Augustus to formally renounce the Polish throne and recognize Stanisław. The regime collapsed when Charles XII was routed at Poltava (1709), allowing Augustus to reclaim the Polish crown; Stanisław went into French exile but later became Duke of Lorraine.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial claims of the Leszczyński regime were coterminous with the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth and are fairly well documented; the extent of actual administrative control beyond Swedish-garrisoned areas is uncertain.
